correctness.rationale: For a consistent partial assignment, surjective feasibility iff missing colours <= unassigned positions. If feasible, an additional forced atom occurs iff there is exactly one missing position and colour. Minimum infeasible partial functions have shortage exactly one and no used singleton colour; same-position contradictory pairs form the only other minimal impossible supports. These three classes exhaust stems and give simultaneous closure in one round. For each stem an atom is exhibited not entailed by any proper subset, showing global minimum cardinality of all simultaneous multi-conclusion direct bases. Ordinary and associated Stirling enumeration gives the formula. For q=3, disjoint infeasible assignment classes and forced near-complete premises yield the claimed closed-set count. Bitmask checker reconstructs model intersections on 149720 finite tested inputs, but infinite validity rests on the proof.

originality.rationale: The generalized stem-minimality result (Wild 2016, Thm. 2) is prior work; it leaves family-specific stem enumeration open. The 2024 direct-basis papers develop general algorithms and comparisons, not an identified exact formula for surjection assignment contexts. The distinguishing theorem is the complete classification of minimally contradictory partial surjections with deficiency one and no singly used colour and the resulting associated-Stirling direct-basis and three-colour closed-set counts for n>q>=3. Existing bijection-only cases do not imply these new multiplicity patterns. This is a provisional best-knowledge originality assessment, not an independent priority certification.

value.rationale: All-surjective assignment constraints provide a natural finite logical context distinct from bijections. The result identifies the exact irreducible premises, including nontrivial repeat-colour deficiency-one contradictions that do not occur in the bijective setting, obtains a sharp all-parameter one-round Horn rule count by associated-Stirling numbers, and derives a complete tricolour closed-set count. These are concrete structural and exact complexity invariants, not mere correctness tests or a generic restatement of stem theory.
